title.narrative: Strengthening Indigenous Conflict Resolution Mechanism amongst tribes in Jos North, Plateau State

description.narrative:
This project seeks to provide an approach to the recurrent crises in Jos and other parts of Plateau state using indigenous conflict resolution mechanisms, known as the restorative justice system, a process which seeks to heal, restore relationships, reconcile and integrate back into the community. This is because life in African cultures is not individualistic but communal as crimes, even when committed against an individual are seen as crimes against the entire community. It is worthy to note that Indigenous conflict resolution practices reflect principles of reconciliation based on long-standing relationships and values, placing highest importance on values for truth, justice, peace, love, harmony, order, balance, reciprocity and sustainability.
This project will therefore impact on men, women and the youths by revisiting some of these indigenous practices and providing an opportunity of applying them to some of the root causes of crises in the State. It will x-ray the various roles these groups have played and can still play in traditional methods of conflict resolution.
This particular project was chosen because of the persistent crises in plateau State which seems to defy current western methods of conflict resolution which often imposes itself on the people and supplants itself on the people’s indigenous mechanisms, values and experiences which are often misunderstood and misinterpreted.
Indigenous conflict resolution mechanisms have proven to be effective and successful in handling some major crises across Africa. These include the Gacaca in Rwanda, Michu and Luba Basa in Ethiopia, Mato Oput in Northern Uganda, the Akobo Peace Conference in Sudan, and one of the world’s most successful traditional peace conferences following Somaliland’s declaration of independence from Somalia in 1991. Finally, the crises of Plateau State have many facets, some of which can lend themselves to traditional reconciliation.
